items.evidence: 26.1.2 worldgen/sculk.rs (727 lines, byte-identical to the 26.1.1 file) has no catalyst_chance/extra_rare_growths decode and no catalyst handling; decode reads only charge_count, amount_per_charge, spread_attempts, growth_rounds, spread_rounds; place() returns Ok(true) at line 163 immediately after the spreader rounds; the string 'catalyst' appears nowhere in the file. Vanilla 26.1.2 SculkPatchFeature.place (fresh javap on the 26.1.2 server-game jar, byte-identical to the 26.1.1 dump): after the spreader rounds, nextFloat() <= catalystChance with a collision-full block below places SCULK_CATALYST at the origin (flag 3), then extraRareGrowths.sample x origin.offset(nextInt(5)-2, 0, nextInt(5)-2) with air above and a face-sturdy block below places SCULK_SHRIEKER[can_summon=true] (flag 3); the catalyst roll happens BEFORE the growth sample, so the missing tail also shifts the RNG stream for features placed after a sculk_patch in the same chunk. 26.1.2 data: sculk_patch_deep_dark catalyst_chance 0.5, extra_rare_growths 0; sculk_patch_ancient_city 0.5, uniform 1..3. The 26.2 tree HAS the tail. Vanilla-side ground truth: the reference world has 364 sculk_catalyst and 179 sculk_shrieker blocks (deep_dark present, 228,190 cells).

items.evidence: The 1.21.7 world comparison measured water -1.04% underground with surface water matching; never root-caused. For 26.1.2 the mechanism is demonstrated, and it is total: the port never constructs a noise-based aquifer (see B6-G09). Pipeline::new reads the 26.3 'aquifers' config object from the noise settings; no 26.1.2 noise settings has that key, so the aquifer is None and generation uses DisabledAquifer - sea-level picker water only, no underground lakes, no flooded caves, no aquifer lava. The 1.21.7 deficit would be far larger in 26.1.2: ALL aquifer water is missing. The aquifer ENGINE itself matches the 26.1.2 jar (noise_based.rs byte-identical to the 26.1.1 file; spot-checked against the 26.1.2 jar: router-form ctor, 13 surface offsets, computeSurfaceLevel with OverworldBiomeBuilder.isDeepDarkRegion, FLOWING_UPDATE_SIMILARITY = 1-44/25); the defect is purely the wiring. Vanilla-side water: 3,666,146 blocks over 7,074 chunks.
items.method: javap + source (re-check of 1.21.7 defect; full aquifer audit)
items.title: Underground water deficit REPRODUCES in 26.1.2: the entire aquifer system is absent (see B6-G09)

items.evidence: Two sites in worldgen/sculk.rs require WATER_SOURCE where the 26.1.2 jar tests fluid-is-water: sculk.rs:305 (attempt_spread_vein, Default branch, non-empty facings) and sculk.rs:548 (can_place_growth above-open gate). Vanilla 26.1.2: SculkBehaviour$1.attemptSpreadVein regrows when the state is air OR fluidState.is(Fluids.WATER); SculkBlock.canPlaceGrowth accepts above air OR (is(WATER) AND fluidState.is(WATER)) (fresh javap on the 26.1.2 jar, byte-identical to the 26.1.1 dumps). The port's WATER_SOURCE is set only for source water (tree_blocks.rs:183-184; flowing water gets WATER_FLUID|ANY_FLUID only), so flowing water blocks sculk vein regrowth and growth placement that vanilla allows. No RNG effect (no random calls in either gate). Same defect as in 26.1, 26.1.1 and 26.2.

items.evidence: Pipeline::new (generator.rs:1115-1119) reads settings_json["aquifers"] - a 26.3 config-object key - and builds the aquifer config from it. NO 26.1.2 noise settings has that key (all 7 checked: overworld, amplified and large_biomes have aquifers_enabled: true; caves, end, floating_islands, nether false; none has 'aquifers'). So the aquifer is always None and generation uses DisabledAquifer: density <= 0 -> the global fluid picker only (sea-level water), no barrier/floodedness/spread noise, no underground lakes or flooded caves. Vanilla 26.1.2 builds NoiseBasedAquifer from the ROUTER (jar ctor takes the NoiseRouter and reads barrierNoise, fluidLevelFloodednessNoise, fluidLevelSpreadNoise, lavaNoise, erosion, depth - fresh javap). The 26.2 tree fixed exactly this (from_router + aquifers_enabled gate, with synthesize::aquifer_exclusion); the 26.1.2 tree has neither from_router nor any aquifer_exclusion synthesis. Silent: no error is raised, the aquifer is just absent. Mechanism behind B6-G03.
items.title: Aquifers entirely disabled: Pipeline::new reads the 26.3 'aquifers' config object, absent from all 26.1.2 settings

items.evidence: worldgen/router.rs declares 8 fields (temperature, vegetation, continents, erosion, depth, ridges, chunk_surface_level, final_density) and from_json requires all of them. The 26.1.2 jar's NoiseRouter record has 15 components (barrier, fluid_level_floodedness, fluid_level_spread, lava, preliminary_surface_level, vein_toggle, vein_ridged, vein_gap, plus the eight) - there is NO chunk_surface_level in 26.1.2 (fresh javap on the 26.1.2 server-game jar: 15 accessor methods). All 7 prepared noise settings lack that key, so NoiseRouter::from_json errors at generator.rs:1093 for every settings object, before the aquifer, rule and spawn-target steps. OverworldGenerator::for_world_with_settings (the real world-construction path) and the flat path both go through Pipeline::new, so no noise or flat world can be constructed. The 26.2 tree has the correct 15-field form (router.rs, ALL: [Self; 15], PreliminarySurfaceLevel). Second failure in the construction cascade (after G06).
items.title: NoiseRouter is the 26.3 eight-field form (requires chunk_surface_level); Pipeline::new fails on 26.1.2 settings

items.evidence: generator.rs:1136-1138: settings_json["material_rule"].as_str() is required, and the name is looked up in the material-rule library. items.evidence: generator.rs:1141-1164 decodes each spawn_target point by mapping every field name through library.named_density(name) - looking up a density function named minecraft:<field>. None of the 7 field names used by the 26.1.2 overworld/amplified/large_biomes spawn targets (continentalness, depth, erosion, humidity, offset, temperature, weirdness) is a registered density function (the 35 registry entries are all minecraft:overworld/..., minecraft:end/..., minecraft:nether/..., minecraft:shift_x, minecraft:shift_z, minecraft:y, minecraft:zero), so the decode errors with 'unknown material density' for every settings object with a non-empty spawn_target. Latent second half: even if the lookups resolved, SpawnTargetPoint::sample_fitness samples each named density, but vanilla's Climate$SpawnFinder.getSpawnPositionAndFitness rebuilds the sampled TargetPoint with depth FORCED to 0 (fresh javap: lconst_0 as the depth argument, bytecode 39) and adds square(offset) as a constant. The 26.1.2 overworld depth function at y=0 is ~1.0 + the offset spline (NOT 0), so sampling it would add a large position-varying bias to every candidate's fitness. The 26.2 tree decodes spawn_target via decode_parameter_point and its spawn_finder zeroes the depth. The radial-search/fitness FORMULA in the port matches the jar exactly; only the decode and the depth handling are wrong.
items.title: spawn_target decode fails (named-density lookups for bare climate field names); depth not zeroed

items.evidence: worldgen/density.rs has no arms for cache_2d, cache_once, flat_cache, shifted_noise, y_clamped_gradient, weird_scaled_sampler or end_islands; the default arm errors 'unknown density type: {kind}' (density.rs:458-462). Recursive census of all 35 density-function files: cache_2d x11, cache_once x12, flat_cache x16, shifted_noise x5, y_clamped_gradient x6, weird_scaled_sampler x3, end_islands x1 - plus surface-rule uses (cache_2d x13, shifted_noise x8, y_clamped_gradient x23 across all 7 settings) and end.json's end_islands. minecraft:overworld/offset is flat_cache > cache_2d > add(...) (with cache_once around blend_alpha inside) - and offset is an argument of minecraft:overworld/depth, a router field, so decoding the router's depth function fails. minecraft:y IS y_clamped_gradient (from_y -4064, to_y 4062 - correcting the 26.1.1 report's -64/320; the data is byte-identical between versions). weird_scaled_sampler x3 in overworld/caves/entrances and spaghetti_2d (the 26.1.2 horizon-core has no WeirdScaledSampler at all; the 26.1 core has it). end_islands x1 in end/sloped_cheese + end.json (the 26.1.2 tree has only the 26.3 name end_outer_islands; the 26.1 tree has both arms). The 26.1.2 tree's minecraft:gradient arm is dead code (no such type in the data). The 26.1 tree has all seven arms; the 26.1.2 compiler even has a ShiftedNoiseSampler (horizon-core/src/density/mod.rs:437) that the JSON decoder never produces. Fires during the router decode in Pipeline::new (after G10's missing-field error, before G11).
items.method: source + jar data, recursive density census (reproduces from 26.1.1)
items.title: Density decode missing cache_2d, cache_once, flat_cache, shifted_noise, y_clamped_gradient, weird_scaled_sampler, end_islands (all used in 26.1.2 data)

items.evidence: Top-level configured-feature types in the 26.1.2 data: 53 distinct, 221 total. Eleven have NO arm in the port's feature dispatch (feature_graph.rs, byte-identical to the 26.1.1 file, plus feature.rs for the end features) - the default arm falls through to BasicFeature::from_json, which errors 'basic feature type' for anything but the three end features: basalt_columns x2, basalt_pillar x1, desert_well x1, dripstone_cluster x1, glowstone_blob x1, kelp x1, nether_forest_vegetation x6, sea_pickle x1, seagrass x4, twisting_vines x2, weeping_vines x1. All except dripstone_cluster have arms in the 26.2 tree (kelp/seagrass/sea_pickle via aquatic.rs, a file absent in 26.1.2; twisting/weeping vines via nether.rs); dripstone_cluster is missing in all three trees (all carry the 26.3 name speleothem_cluster instead). Plus coral_mushroom, nested inside warm_ocean_vegetation's simple_random_selector (dispatch has coral_tree|coral_claw only; CoralFeature::decode errors on other kinds). Total: 22 broken configured features, affecting 24 placed features (verified by name against the 26.1.2 placed-feature data). Also missing: the nether_cave carver arm (carver/generation.rs has cave + canyon only, byte-identical to 26.1.1; 26.2 has cave | nether_cave); the 5 nether biomes list minecraft:nether_cave as their carver. Overlap with G15: 6 of the 22 also use long-form state providers; union G14+G15 is 126 of 221 configured features.

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 density is double throughout: DensityFunction.compute returns double, fillArray(double[], ...) (fresh javap on the 26.1.2 server-game jar); Biome's three noises are PerlinSimplexNoise with getValue(DDZ)D. The 26.1.2 port computes the same pipeline in f32 at four sites: (1) density graph - horizon-core/src/density/graph/mod.rs GraphNode::Constant(f32), Gradient/Clamp/Choice f32 fields, all samplers return Result<f32, SampleError> (26.1 core is f64 throughout); (2) climate fields - worldgen/climate.rs from_values([f32; 6]), fields [Vec<f32>; 6] (vanilla samples in double then casts to float for Climate.quantizeCoord; 26.1 tree: from_values([f64; 6])); (3) blending - worldgen/blending.rs NO_VALUE: f32 = f32::MAX, heights/densities f32 (vanilla BlendingData.NO_VALUE is double - fresh javap on the 26.1.2 jar; the port's own comment at blending.rs:21 cites Float.MAX_VALUE, wrong for 26.1.2; 26.1 tree: f64::MAX); (4) biome temperature noises - worldgen/biome_temperature.rs uses f32 SimplexNoise/NoiseStack (seeds 1234/3456/2345) where vanilla uses double PerlinSimplexNoise; the 26.1.2 horizon-core has no PerlinSimplexNoise at all (the 26.1 tree added it). Effect is rounding-level per sample; magnitude unmeasured statically (B6-H arbitrates). The 26.1 tree is the repair template for all four sites.
items.method: javap + source diff vs the 26.1 tree (reproduces from 26.1.1)
items.title: Worldgen numeric pipeline is f32 where vanilla 26.1.2 computes in f64 (density graph, climate, blending, biome temperature noises)

items.evidence: Generate port chunks at seed 4656297851632877335 (the reference world's seed, confirmed from data/minecraft/world_gen_settings.dat) and compare against the vanilla reference world (~/workspace/vanilla-world-mc/26.1.2/26_1_2/, 7,074 chunks). STAGE RULE: the port's generate_proto output is terrain-level (biomes, noise fill, aquifers, material surface, carvers - the 26.1.2 statuses up to CARVERS); vanilla region files are post-decorate. Compare post-decorate to post-decorate for blocks, terrain-level to terrain-level for density. Direct comparison is only valid where structure templates contain no air (ancient city: 0 air) - trial chambers/villages carve air during placement, so a terrain-vs-post-decorate gap there is a measurement artifact, not a density bug (the 1.21.7 -6.4 'beardifier residual' was exactly this). B6-H arbitrates: G02/G04 live confirmation, G03's magnitude once aquifers exist, the sculk/G07/G08 RNG-stream effects, and the G17 f32 magnitude. Blocked until the construction cascade (G06/G10/G13/G11/G12) is fixed - no port world can be generated today.

items.title: Paired port-vs-vanilla chunk comparison for 26.1.2 (stage rule applies)

method: javap -c -p on the named 26.1.2 server-game jar for every vanilla method spot-checked (SculkPatchFeature, SculkBehaviour/SculkBlock/SculkSpreader/ChargeCursor, SnowLayerBlock.canSurvive, Biome.shouldSnow/shouldFreeze/coldEnoughToSnow + PerlinSimplexNoise fields, Aquifer$NoiseBasedAquifer incl. ctor, Climate$SpawnFinder/ParameterPoint, NoiseRouter (15 components), DensityFunction, Feature, ConfiguredFeature, ChunkStatus, BlendingData.NO_VALUE); exact data diffs of prepared resources vs jar (715 populated registry entries; structure NBTs 1202/1202; flat presets 9/9 + visible tag; multi-noise presets); vanilla 26.1.2 reference world census with an own NBT parser (seed 4656297851632877335, 7,074 chunks, block/biome/structure census, snow-on-packed-ice 0 world-wide); decode-coverage audit of every worldgen dispatch arm against the jar data (dispatch tables are the authority, not string presence; recursive density census supersedes the audit's non-recursive glob); Batch 0 oracle-status triage for all 57 oracles referenced by the batch's 64 drivers (18 pass / 39 fail). No driver was run: 9 drivers have passing oracles and 17 have no oracle (ready when the execution block lifts); 38 are blocked on failing oracles. Checks tally = 27 behaviour checks only (19 pass, 8 gap); oracle triage counted separately per the 26.1 convention.
name: Worldgen / features
out_of_scope_failures: None. Adjacent findings NOT recorded as B6 defects: (1) DUMMY block entities (42) in the reference world - vanilla-side oddity, BEs owned by another batch; (2) the tag() silent-empty footgun (missing tag -> empty set, no error) is the mechanism behind G07; it is a robustness gap in the shared survival/tag loader, not a worldgen defect per se (all tags used by the verified snow path are present in the prepared data); (3) the 26.1.2 level/sculk.rs reads the absent sculk_growth_inhibitors tag at :620 (dead cap in live gameplay) and narrows the water gate to sources at :611 - same patterns as G07/G05, in B4's live-sculk scope; (4) the port's ChunkStatus enum is the 26.3 form (single TERRAIN, no NOISE/SURFACE/CARVERS) but behaviourally inert - generate_proto performs all three 26.1.2 stages in one call, and the only NBT use is retrogen target_status, which no reference-world chunk carries (0 of 7,074 chunks with retrogen/blending data); the 26.1, 26.1.1 and 26.2 trees have the identical enum; (5) generator.rs tests still reference a 26.3 prepared-data dir (../../.local/horizon-client/26.3) in several test paths (lines 4077, 4116, 4309) - test-only; (6) dripstone_cluster is missing in the 26.1.2, 26.1.1, 26.1 and 26.2 trees (all carry the 26.3 name speleothem_cluster instead); (7) VanillaSteppedInterpolationOracle (16 errors, new file replacing the passing VanillaInterpolationOracle) and its driver test_stepped_interpolation_parity are out of the B6 driver set by the keyword rule; (8) the 4 non-B6 newly-failing oracles in Batch 0's G10 group (VanillaBlockTransformerOracle, VanillaBrewingFuelOracle, VanillaFillLayerOracle, VanillaReplaceBlockOracle) belong to their batches; (9) the 9 runnable + 17 no-oracle drivers were not run (execution block) - they are unmeasured, not passing; (10) NEW in the 26.1.1->26.1.2 delta (chunk NBT, not worldgen): chunk.rs dropped the legacy palette reader (from_palette_nbt, Name/Properties form) and from_nbt now reads only the strict id/properties form, while vanilla 26.1.2 still writes Name/Properties palettes (verified in the reference world) - flagged for the owning batch, not minted here.
source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 6 — checks + triage only, no fixes. Scope: noise/density functions, carvers, configured/placed features, structures and structure sets, template pools, biomes and biome sources, chunk generation stages, spawn finding, world presets. Static checks only (javap + source + data diffs + vanilla world census); no cargo builds, no driver runs, no commits.
systemic_note: Two systemic causes, both 26.3-form carry-over. (1) The 26.1.2 tree carries 26.3 forms where 26.1.2 uses the 1.21.x forms - the prepare folder names (G06), the NoiseRouter (G10), the aquifer config object (G09), the material-rule name (G11), the spawn-target named densities (G12), the density cache/shifted-noise arms (G13), 11 feature types + the nether carver (G14), the state-provider short names (G15), and the missing random_offset arm (G16). The 26.2 tree is the repair template for G06/G09-G14; the merged 26.1 tree is the repair template for G13's three extra arms, G15 and G16. (2) The 26.1.2 tree's numeric pipeline is f32 where vanilla is f64 (G17) - density graph, climate fields, blending data, biome temperature noises; the 26.1 tree is the repair template. The sculk defects (G01/G05/G07/G08) are the exception: same narrow-predicate pattern as 26.2's G05, found only by javap-diffing the feature's gates. Arm presence is not correctness - G05, G07 and G08 were silent narrowings inside present arms, and G15's audit 'ok' for simple_state_provider/weighted_state_provider was a false positive from an unrelated file (litho.rs); this run adds two more of the same class (seagrass grep-ok with no dispatch arm; fortress spawn overrides in the structure audit). Three of the four 1.21.7 defects reproduce in 26.1.2 (G01, G03, G05); only G02 and G04 are withdrawn. The 26.1.2 port is the 26.1.1 port verbatim on worldgen: no 26.1.2 world can generate at all with the current tree + prepared data, and 126 of 221 configured features cannot decode (G14+G15 union).
